evidence.note: At every validation checkpoint the agent tracked the compressed checkpoint size (~28.8MB), continuously confirming the 32MB byte cap rather than trusting it once.

Final verification script imports train_AGENT.py, loads the compressed checkpoint through load_model_for_verification (the grader's own entry point), checks file size, and validates the forward/loss contract — end-to-end through the actual interface.

Reloaded the quantized checkpoint and computed local bpb = 0.98343, recognized it exceeded 0.983, and resumed training. This demonstrates treating local val_bpb from the dequantized checkpoint as a calibrated proxy against the real threshold, and catching a near-miss before submission.

Re-verified after fine-tuning and bigram augmentation: reload via load_model_for_verification, loss contract satisfied, size 30.27MB under cap, local bpb 0.97891 — repeated the full contract+size+bpb check as the plan/checkpoint changed.
Repeatedly reasoned that the ~0.004 local margin was small relative to the stated ~0.05 hidden/local bpb variance, showing explicit awareness of proxy noise and desire for threshold margin.

reasoning: The agent verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification), reloads the quantized checkpoint to confirm int8 dequant round-trips and compute local bpb, checks the loss contract, tracks size against the 32MB cap throughout, and explicitly treats local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin awareness against 0.983 — matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because it tested only one of the two load paths, never asserted logits depend on position or ran a shifted-pass bpb harness, and verification was a manual final-stage gate rather than an automated regression harness run every iteration.
